## Motivation

- DeepSeek-V4 keeps two kinds of KV for a cached prefix: the full KV (compressed entries and indexer keys) and a smaller sliding-window (SWA) KV. Under memory pressure the SWA KV of an idle prefix is evicted first.
- On main, a request that reuses such a prefix gets no cache hit. It prefills the whole prefix again even though the full KV is still on the GPU.
- This PR rebuilds the SWA KV instead. It replays only the last tokens of the prefix (5,632 for V4-Flash) and reads everything older from the cached full KV.
- On a 120K-token prompt the request after an eviction takes 0.21 s instead of 2.21 s.
- This is a smaller take on #31713 by @jellysnack. The replay length and the "at least twice the replay length" threshold come from that PR.

## Modifications

- New server flag `--enable-swa-recompute`, off by default.
- Replay length: `ceil_align(ceil_align(W, page) + (L - 1) * W, page)` for window `W` and `L` layers. Layer `l` needs window rows built from layer `l - 1`, one window further back each time, so only the last window of the replay is exact and only that window is kept.
- Cache side (`unified_cache/swa_recompute.py`):
  - A match reports how many full-KV tokens a replay would make reusable. Prefixes that would save less than twice the replay length are prefilled again as before.
  - When the request is admitted, fresh SWA rows are bound to the replayed tokens and the last window is attached to the tree. The other rows are scratch and are freed after the forward.
  - The scratch rows are freed with the page-aligned segment free, which does not call `torch.unique`.
- Worker side (`model_executor/swa_recompute.py`):
  - The replay is one extra extend forward over the replayed tokens, run before the request's normal extend.
  - It writes SWA rows and the 4x compressor state, which lives beside the SWA rows. It does not store compressed or indexer entries, so the cached full KV is not touched.
  - Window slots before the replay start are masked with the existing `swa_replay_start` floor.
  - The prefill CUDA graph is not used for the replay.
- DSpark: the draft keeps its own SWA rows. They are rebuilt from the replay's captured hidden states through the existing prefill injection path.
- The flag is refused at startup with DeepSeek-V4.1, DP attention, context parallelism, pipeline parallelism, PD disaggregation, the TRT-LLM attention backend, the unified KV layout, unified memory, online C128 compression, two-batch overlap, mixed chunks, HiSparse, LoRA, radix sessions, the external cache linker, speculative decoding other than DSpark, SM120 and non-CUDA hardware.
- Docs: a row in the server arguments table and a section in the DeepSeek-V4 cookbook.
- Tests: the request stubs in `test_prefill_adder.py` and `test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py` and the forward-batch stubs in `test_dsv41_late_layer_tail_readers.py` and `test_encoder_swa_replay.py` get the new replay fields, because the scheduler and the attention backend now read them.

Differences from #31713:

1. A server flag instead of an environment variable.
2. The replay binds fresh SWA rows through the normal full-to-SWA mapping. There is no private-page routing in the planner or the attention kernels, and no change to the compress-plan JIT kernel.
3. DSpark is supported.
4. HiCache is not covered. Only full KV that is on the GPU is reused.

## Accuracy Tests

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` on 4x B300. The check is the repo's cache-hit KL helper, `test_input_output_logprobs_match_prefill_cache_hit_helper`, run on 8 LongBench-v2 prompts of 13,436 to 26,739 tokens with 512 new tokens. The helper's default prompt length is 3,000 tokens, which is too short to rebuild, so the prompts were cut at 12,000 to 36,000 tokens instead. It prefills each prompt, generates from the cache hit, and compares the output logprobs with a cold prefill of the same tokens.

The squeezed pool has 12,800 SWA rows, so each prompt's SWA KV is evicted by the next prompt. The intact pool keeps every prompt's SWA KV.

```bash
# rebuild, squeezed SWA pool
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.032 --max-running-requests 1 --enable-swa-recompute

# rebuild with DSpark, squeezed SWA pool
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.032 --max-running-requests 1 --enable-swa-recompute --speculative-algorithm DSPARK

# intact cache
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.5 --max-running-requests 1 --enable-swa-recompute

# intact cache with DSpark
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.5 --max-running-requests 1 --enable-swa-recompute --speculative-algorithm DSPARK

# flag off, squeezed SWA pool
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.032 --max-running-requests 1
```

| Server | Prompts with a cache hit | Hits through the rebuild | Average KL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rebuild, squeezed pool | 8/8 | 7 | 0.0046 |
| Rebuild with DSpark, squeezed pool | 8/8 | 7 | 0.0063 |
| Intact cache | 8/8 | 0 | 0.0048 |
| Intact cache with DSpark | 8/8 | 0 | 0.0054 |
| Flag off, squeezed pool | 0/8 | 0 | not computed |

- Each row is one run. This model is not reproducible run to run at these prompt lengths. Earlier runs of the intact row on the same prompts gave 0.0036 to 0.0059, and a cold run with DSpark and no cache hit gave 0.0071, so the rebuild rows are within noise of the intact rows.
- The last prompt is never evicted, so it is a normal hit in every row.
- No scheduler exceptions in any run.
- I merged main into this branch thirteen times to clear conflicts, and ran the rebuild rows again after each merge. Every run gave 8/8 hits and no scheduler exceptions, with average KL between 0.0027 and 0.0056. The latest run, after merging main at `3c560089e1`, gave 0.0052 with DSpark. The third merge (`943621c336`) needed code changes: main had renamed `MatchResult.device_indices` to `device_prefix_len`, and now gives the draft model its write locations through `kv_loc_plan`, so the rebuild code uses both.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same model and hardware. A 120,000-token prompt A is prefilled, a second 120,000-token prompt evicts A's SWA KV, and A is sent again. This is repeated four more times. Numbers are time to first token.

```bash
# flag on
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 300000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.032 --max-running-requests 8 --enable-swa-recompute

# flag off
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 300000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.032 --max-running-requests 8
```

The no-DSpark row uses the flag-on command without `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`.

| Server | Cold prefill | Hit, SWA KV intact | Hit after SWA eviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flag off, DSpark | 2.21 s | 0.10 to 0.14 s | 2.21 s (prefilled again) |
| Flag on, DSpark | 2.21 s | 0.10 to 0.14 s | 0.21 s |
| Flag on, no DSpark | 2.19 s | 0.10 to 0.12 s | 0.21 s |

- One server run per row. The "after eviction" number is the same within 0.01 s over the last four cycles. The first rebuild after server start takes 0.26 s.
- The rebuild costs about 0.1 s more than an intact hit. That is the replay forward over 5,632 tokens.
- After each of the thirteen merges, the flag-on DSpark row was run again: 0.21 to 0.24 s after eviction and 2.19 to 2.25 s cold. The latest run, after merging main at `3c560089e1`, gave 0.21 s after eviction and 2.20 to 2.25 s cold.
- Unit tests after merging main at `14ad64c411`: `test/registered/unit/{mem_cache,managers,server_args,model_executor,spec,layers,disaggregation,scripted_runtime,observability,api,dllm,multimodal}` and `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4.py` on one B300 give the same 335 failures and 12 errors on this branch and on main. The 2 extra failures this merge brought in were main tests whose forward-batch stubs lack `swa_recompute`. This branch adds the field to those stubs and they pass. After merging main at `3671503e44`, I ran `test/registered/unit/{model_executor,layers,mem_cache,managers,server_args}` again. The only conflict was in `test_encoder_swa_replay.py`, where main moved the forward-batch stub into a shared helper; the helper now sets `swa_recompute=False`. After merging main at `3c560089e1`, the same five directories and `test_deepseek_v4.py` give the same 295 failures and 12 errors on this branch and on main. The only conflict was in `schedule_batch.py`: main added `resets_swa_window()` for the same check this branch had written inline, so the branch now calls it.

 Two further limits are worth knowing before you size a run. The pool is a per-node process, so a worker that spans nodes would shard its keyspace by node. And under PD disaggregation the §3.7 pairs run the linker on the prefill role only, so the decode worker offloads nothing; in aggregated serving the single worker offloads its own KV.
+
+### 3.9 SWA Recompute (Experimental)
+
+DeepSeek-V4 keeps two kinds of KV for a cached prefix: the full KV and a smaller sliding-window (SWA) KV sized by `--swa-full-tokens-ratio`. Under memory pressure the SWA KV of an idle prefix is evicted first. A later request that reuses that prefix then has to prefill it again, even though its full KV is still cached.
+
+`--enable-swa-recompute` rebuilds the SWA KV instead. The server replays only the last tokens of the prefix (5,632 tokens for V4-Flash at the default page size of 256) and reads everything older from the cached full KV. Prefixes shorter than about twice that length are prefilled again as before.
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+  --trust-remote-code \
+  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
+  --tp 4 \
+  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \

+  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \

+

+"""Cache side of DeepSeek-V4 SWA recompute: bind fresh SWA rows to a FULL
+prefix that outlived its window, for the worker's replay to fill."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.swa import SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.unified_hybrid_swa import UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import EvictParams, MatchPrefixParams
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixKey
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import ceil_align
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.unified_tree_core_interface import NodeId
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedRadixCache
+
+# A replay costs about a prefill of swa_recompute_len tokens; prefixes that
+# save less than twice that are prefilled again instead.
+_MIN_GAIN_RATIO = 2
+
+
+def swa_recompute_len(*, sliding_window: int, num_layers: int, page_size: int) -> int:
+    """Tokens to replay so every layer's last window is exact: layer ``l`` reads
+    window rows built from layer ``l - 1`` outputs, one window further back each."""
+    return ceil_align(
+        ceil_align(sliding_window, page_size) + (num_layers - 1) * sliding_window,
+        page_size,
+    )
+
+
+class SWARecompute(msgspec.Struct):
+    # First prefix position the worker replays; page-aligned.
+    start: int
+    # FULL ids from ``start`` whose SWA rows only the replay reads; freed after the forward.
+    workspace: torch.Tensor
+    # False once a batch took the replay.
+    pending: bool = True
+
+    def take_start(self) -> Optional[int]:
+        pending, self.pending = self.pending, False
+        return self.start if pending else None
+
+
+def supports_swa_recompute(allocator) -> bool:
+    return (
+        isinstance(allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator)
+        and not isinstance(allocator, UnifiedSWAAllocatorBase)
+        and not allocator.swa_req_ring
+    )
+
+
+def _recomputable_full_len(
+    cache: UnifiedRadixCache, key: RadixKey, matched_len: int
+) -> tuple[int, Optional[NodeId]]:
+    """Device FULL length a replay can reach from ``matched_len``, else ``matched_len``."""
+    replay_len = cache.swa_recompute_len
+    window = ceil_align(cache.sliding_window_size, cache.page_size)
+    full_len, node_id, _ = cache.tree_core.match_full_device_prefix(key)
+    full_len = full_len // cache.page_size * cache.page_size
+    if full_len - matched_len < _MIN_GAIN_RATIO * replay_len:
+        return matched_len, None
+    window_start = full_len - window
+    if cache.tree_core.swa_tombstone_ranges(key, window_start, full_len) != [
+        (window_start, full_len)
+    ]:
+        return matched_len, None
+    return full_len, node_id
+
+
+def swa_recompute_hit_length(
+    cache: UnifiedRadixCache, key: RadixKey, matched_len: int, full_kv_hit_length: int
+) -> int:
+    # full_kv_hit_length also counts host FULL, so it only bounds the gain.
+    if full_kv_hit_length - matched_len < _MIN_GAIN_RATIO * cache.swa_recompute_len:
+        return 0
+    full_len, _ = _recomputable_full_len(cache, key, matched_len)
+    return full_len - matched_len
+
+
+def init_swa_recompute(
+    cache: UnifiedRadixCache, req: Req, key: RadixKey
+) -> Optional[tuple[int, NodeId, SWARecompute]]:
+    """Bind fresh SWA rows behind the FULL prefix and publish its last window.
+    The window holds no data until the returned replay runs, so the request must
+    enter the batch being built."""
+    matched_len = req.prefix_len
+    full_len, node_id = _recomputable_full_len(cache, key, matched_len)
+    if node_id is None:
+        return None

I merged main into this branch because it had a conflict in `schedule_batch.py`.

- main removed `Req.prefix_indices` and `Req.extend_range` (#42822, #42824, #42825) and moved the cache match into `match_kv_cache`. The replay bookkeeping now lives in `match_kv_cache` and uses `req.prefix_len`.
- The scheduler unit tests in `test/registered/unit/managers` failed on this PR because their request stubs did not have the new replay fields. I added the fields to the stubs and the tests pass again.
- I ran the two rebuild rows of the accuracy table and the two flag-on rows of the timing table again on the merged branch. The results are in the PR description and match the earlier runs.

Merged main at `943621c336` to clear a conflict. Two things in main had changed under this PR, so the rebuild code was updated:

- `MatchResult.device_indices` is now `device_prefix_len`.
- The DSpark draft model now gets its write locations from `kv_loc_plan`, so the replay passes its own plan.

The DSpark rebuild row was run again after the merge: 8/8 hits, average KL 0.0040, 0.22 s after eviction against 2.21 s cold, no scheduler exceptions. The description has the numbers.

Main has changed next to this PR almost every day this week, so I have kept merging it in. After the latest merge (`9c7b338a19`) the rebuild check still gives 8/8 hits with average KL 0.0027, 0.21 s after eviction against 2.21 s cold, and the same unit test results as main.
